config.title: Build typed feature flag variants

intro.title: Build typed feature flag variants
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple system to manage typed feature flag variants, which are settings that control different versions of a feature in an application. You will learn how to use TypeScript's union types to define a set of allowed string values, ensuring that only valid variants can be used. The core programming concept involves creating a type-safe configuration object to store and access these variants. By the end, you will have a reusable, error-resistant way to handle feature toggles in your TypeScript projects.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are essential in modern applications for controlled rollouts and A/B testing. In e-commerce platforms, they enable gradual release of new checkout flows or payment methods. SaaS dashboards use them to toggle between different analytics views or experimental UI layouts. Developers implement typed variants to safely manage beta features, premium tiers, or region-specific functionality while preventing runtime errors.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the structure of feature flag variants
Implement a typed configuration object that stores feature flag states
Initialize a feature flag manager with proper TypeScript type annotations
Apply conditional logic to control feature visibility based on flag states
Manipulate feature flag values to toggle features on and off
Integrate typed feature flags into a sample application component
Configure a type-safe function to check feature flag availability
